- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to avoid missing early reversal.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in 3–5 day window.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in bearish sentiment periods; add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment <0.33 for 3+ days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often lags; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of actual trend direction.
